d.d: An indefinite, but usually small, number of.
d.x: There are a few cars (=some, but a relatively small number) in the street.

d.d: Not many; a small (in comparison with another number stated or implied) but somewhat indefinite number of.
d.x: Very few did she have not to go there, did she?

d.d: Obscuring one to two oktas (eighths) of the sky.
d.x: Tonight: A few clouds. Increasing cloudiness overnight.
Many are called, but few are chosen.

d.d: comparative degree of few; a smaller number.
d.x: Fewer women wear hats these days.

d.d: Less; a smaller amount of something non-integral commonly expressed as an integer
superlative degree of few; the smallest number.
d.x: On Sundays, the fewest cars use this street.
